## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/46799

HiCache normally registers its host pools with CUDA. On the tested Confidential Computing (CC) host, `cudaHostRegister` returns error 801 (`cudaErrorNotSupported`), preventing the default host-pool allocation path from working. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next also needs its GDN recurrent state and QSA indexer pools to follow the same allocation policy as attention KV.

Add an opt-in pageable L2 host tier so these deployments can extend prefix caching to CPU memory.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_HICACHE_PAGEABLE=1` to allocate attention KV, recurrent-state, and QSA host pools in ordinary CPU memory. Pinned allocation remains the default.
- Add staged MLA/DSA backup and load for `direct` I/O with `page_first_direct` layout. CUDA runtime copies move data between host and device; GPU kernels access only device buffers. Transfers preserve page order and packed indexer scales, and teardown releases staging buffers and MLA transfer views.
- Support DSV4 whole-page transfers and partial-token transfers for the C4 V4 layout (64 slots per 37,440-byte row) through pageable copies. Partial copies preserve neighboring values, scales, and page padding.
- Reject kernel I/O, unified memory, external cache linkers, HiSparse, and L3 storage when pageable mode is enabled. The L3 check also applies to runtime attachment.
- Fix the SM90 FlashInfer GDN fallback so CUDA graph padding uses the reserved dummy state slot instead of overwriting the last live slot. This fix is also included in [#46554](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46554).

Host sizing and eviction continue to use existing HiCache policies. Pageable copies may synchronize the submitting thread. MLA/DSA staging adds temporary allocations outside the host-pool budget.

## Accuracy Tests

### Standard decoding

Tests use `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` from ModelScope, revision `47b13b2ed4`, on an H20 host running as a TDX guest. The reference and HiCache instances each use two GPUs with TP2/EP2. Both use FlashInfer GDN prefill/decode, BF16 recurrent state, a 32,768-token context and device KV limit, chunked prefill 2,048, 16 Mamba state slots, and a static memory fraction of 0.96. The requested running-request limit is 4; the runtime caps it at 3 because each request requires five state slots. CUDA graphs and overlap scheduling are enabled. MTP and PLE embedding offload are disabled. HiCache uses `write_through`, direct I/O, `page_first_direct`, and a host/device ratio of 4.

GSM8K follows the [upstream Qwen3.8 test recipe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6393e66b8649b4e6e22f2d94a933e69059192900/test/registered/e2e/disaggregation/test_qwen4_exp_pd_prefill_cp.py): `run_sgl_eval`, 200 questions, 32 client threads, thinking enabled, and a 16,384-token output limit. The evaluator uses temperature 0 and top_p 0.95. Both instances exceed that test's 94% threshold. The upstream test uses NVFP4; these paired results use the same FP8 checkpoint.

| Test | Reference without HiCache | Pageable HiCache |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | 195/200 (97.5%) | 195/200 (97.5%) |
| Request errors / output truncations | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Known-answer retrieval, ~2.5k-token prefix | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Known-answer retrieval, ~20k-token prefix | 3/3 | 3/3 |

The retrieval test places an access code at 10%, 50%, or 90% of the prompt. The reference keeps the prefix in device cache; unrelated requests evict the HiCache instance’s device copy before retrieval. All cases returned the expected code. HiCache reloaded 2,496 host tokens per short-prefix request and 20,032 per long-prefix request.

Regression results: 168 passed, one Mamba kernel-I/O test skipped (unused by pageable mode), and five DSV4 L2 tests passed.

Coverage includes allocation and cleanup, configuration checks, runtime L3 attachment, storage registration/DCP behavior, and GDN padding. CUDA transfer tests check:

- MLA/DSA byte-exact backup/load through host-pool dispatch, release of backing and staging buffers, and repeated `destroy()`.
- DSV4 whole pages and C4 V4 partial-token transfers across chunk boundaries, including preservation of adjacent data and rejection of invalid device indices.
- QSA uint8/bfloat16 compressed buffers and scattered pages on a non-default stream, with byte-exact backup/load and teardown without host registration.

The branch starts from `6393e66b86`. Standard-decoding Qwen measurements use `9ee3850a87`, GLM measurements use `a4e8b21ef0`, and DeepSeek measurements use `7e5306ca76`. Regression results correspond to `4d361847c3`.

For the standard-decoding Qwen tests, run GSM8K once per endpoint, with separate output directories:

```bash
python test/manual/hicache/eval_pageable_accuracy.py \
  --url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model "$MODEL_PATH" --output-dir "$RESULT_DIR"

python test/manual/hicache/eval_pageable_roundtrip.py \
  --url "$HICACHE_URL" --reference-url "$REFERENCE_URL" \
  --model "$MODEL_PATH" --churn-requests 16 --prompt-tokens 20000 \
  --output "$RESULT_DIR/reload.json"
```

### Speculative decoding

MTP/DSpark tests use `4d361847c3` on the H20 CC host. Each pair uses the same checkpoint and speculative configuration, with HiCache disabled in the reference.

| Model / speculative configuration | GSM8K without HiCache | Pageable HiCache | Long-prefix L2 reload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4/EP4, NEXTN 3/1/4 | 192/200 (96.0%) | 195/200 (97.5%) | 3/3 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, TP8/EP8, DSPARK block size 5 | 194/200 (97.0%) | 195/200 (97.5%) | 3/3 |
| GLM-5.3-W4AFP8, TP8, EAGLE 5/1/6 | 1284/1319 (97.35%) | 1287/1319 (97.57%) | 3/3 |

All six runs passed the upstream accuracy thresholds with zero request errors. The DeepSeek and GLM reference runs each had one truncated response, counted incorrect; the pageable runs had none. All ~20k-token reload cases returned the expected answer with a host-cache hit. DeepSeek used eager metadata preparation after the upstream metadata graph capture failed in both configurations; target-verify and draft CUDA graphs remained active.

Use the same checkpoint, GPUs, backends, and KV capacity for both runs. Define the shared model and serving arguments in the Bash array `SERVER_ARGS`, including `--enable-cache-report` and `--max-total-tokens 32768`. Add the model’s speculative flags:

```bash
# Qwen3.8 (TP4/EP4)
--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
# DeepSeek-V4.1 (TP8/EP8)
--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
# GLM-5.3 (TP8)
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
```

First launch the reference with `SGLANG_HICACHE_PAGEABLE=0 python -m sglang.launch_server "${SERVER_ARGS[@]}"`, without `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, and save its results:

```bash
# PROFILE: qwen38 | dsv41 | glm53
# MODEL_PATH: local checkpoint directory
# SERVED_MODEL: API model name; ENDPOINT_URL: running server URL
python test/manual/hicache/eval_pageable_accuracy.py \
  --profile "$PROFILE" --url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model "$SERVED_MODEL" \
  --output-dir "$RESULT_DIR/reference-gsm8k"
python test/manual/hicache/eval_pageable_serial_roundtrip.py \
  --url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model "$MODEL_PATH" --mode reference \
  --require-speculative --output "$RESULT_DIR/reference-reload.json"
```

Stop the reference server, then launch the pageable configuration and evaluate it using the same checkpoint path and saved reference:

```bash
SGLANG_HICACHE_PAGEABLE=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  "${SERVER_ARGS[@]}" \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --enable-cache-report \
  --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \
  --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-ratio 4

python test/manual/hicache/eval_pageable_accuracy.py \
  --profile "$PROFILE" --url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model "$SERVED_MODEL" \
  --output-dir "$RESULT_DIR/pageable-gsm8k"
python test/manual/hicache/eval_pageable_serial_roundtrip.py \
  --url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model "$MODEL_PATH" --mode pageable \
  --require-speculative --reference-result "$RESULT_DIR/reference-reload.json" \
  --output "$RESULT_DIR/pageable-reload.json"
```

The GSM8K profiles use upstream scoring and generation settings, with 200 questions and a 94% threshold for Qwen, 200/95% for DeepSeek, and 1,319/92% for GLM. The reload script uses ~20k-token prompts and 16 churn requests. The scheduler caps output length to fit the available KV capacity.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Performance measurements below use standard decoding with MTP/DSpark disabled. The Qwen benchmark uses upstream `sglang.bench_serving` with `generated-shared-prefix`: 32 groups, four requests per group, nominal 2,048-token shared prefixes, 128-token questions and 128 output tokens, seed 42, concurrency 4, and unlimited request rate. With client concurrency 4 and an effective running-request limit of 3, one request may queue. Each configuration runs serially once, with four warmup requests followed by a cache flush and 128 measured requests. Both runs process the same 285,986 input tokens after tokenization.

| Configuration | Completed | Output tokens/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Device-cache hit tokens | Host-cache hit tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reference without HiCache | 128/128 | 161.22 | 637.76 | 11.56 | 21,312 | 0 |
| Pageable HiCache | 128/128 | 159.48 | 691.35 | 11.60 | 23,360 | 95,168 |

Both configurations use the standard-decoding Qwen server settings above. The runtime skips unavailable FlashInfer all-reduce fusion in this CC environment and uses the default MoE tuning configuration.

```bash
python -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --backend sglang --base-url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
  --gsp-num-groups 32 --gsp-prompts-per-group 4 \
  --gsp-system-prompt-len 2048 --gsp-question-len 128 --gsp-output-len 128 \
  --gsp-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 4 \
  --warmup-requests 4 --flush-cache --seed 42 --cache-report \
  --output-details --output-file "$RESULT_FILE"
```

### GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Additional checks use the same shared-prefix protocol on eight H20 GPUs in the CC guest, with a 32,768-token device KV limit and no MTP. The pageable configuration uses direct I/O, `page_first_direct`, `write_through`, and ratio 4. Each model has its own generated dataset; the paired runs process 290,254 input tokens for GLM and 284,905 for DeepSeek.

| Model / checkpoint | Configuration | Completed | Output tokens/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Host-cache hit tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 | Reference without HiCache | 128/128 | 142.10 | 1530.11 | 16.92 | 0 |
| GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 | Pageable HiCache | 128/128 | 169.64 | 725.30 | 16.76 | 116,160 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 | Reference without HiCache | 128/128 | 230.51 | 912.44 | 10.18 | 0 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 | Pageable HiCache | 128/128 | 246.71 | 591.02 | 10.21 | 112,640 |

Both use chunked prefill 2,048 and a running-request limit of 32. Overlap scheduling and decode CUDA graphs are enabled. GLM also uses prefill graphs; upstream's DSV4 policy disables prefill graphs due to capture-pool memory pressure. Unavailable multicast/allreduce fusion falls back in both configurations.

All 768 measured requests completed successfully with 128 output tokens each. Host-cache hits confirm L2 reuse. Each configuration was measured once on a shared host using the native SGLang API.

## Checklist

- [x] Run the repository's pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add allocator, configuration, lifecycle, and CUDA transfer tests.
- [x] Update deployment documentation; validate its build and links.
- [x] Run paired Qwen3.8 GSM8K and forced L2 reload tests.
- [x] Complete and review serving performance sanity checks.
- [x] Report model revision, configuration, and validation scope.
- [x] Validate Qwen3.8 MTP, DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark, and GLM-5.3 MTP with paired GSM8K and forced L2 reload tests.

+## Pageable host memory in Confidential Computing deployments
+
+On CUDA Confidential Computing (CC) hosts that cannot register host memory,
+set `SGLANG_HICACHE_PAGEABLE=1` and use the direct I/O backend:
+
+```bash
+SGLANG_HICACHE_PAGEABLE=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path /models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
+  --tp-size 2 --ep-size 2 --no-ple-offload-embedding \
+  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
+  --hicache-io-backend direct \
+  --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct
+```
+
+This mode allocates ordinary CPU memory for attention KV, recurrent state,
+and QSA indexer host pools. It does not call `cudaHostRegister` or unregister
+those allocations during cleanup. Copies use the CUDA runtime rather than
+kernels that access host pointers. MLA and DSA pools use device staging for
+backup and CPU gathering followed by device scatter for load-back.
+DSV4 pools stage whole-page transfers on the device. Partial-token transfers support the C4 V4 layout
+(64 slots per 37,440-byte row). They copy values and scales separately,
+preserving neighboring slots and page padding. These copies use bounded chunks and synchronize the submitting
+thread before CPU memory is read or written.
+
+Pageable mode supports the L2 host tier. Kernel I/O, unified memory, L3 storage,
+external cache linkers, and HiSparse are rejected.
+The L3 restriction also applies to runtime storage attachment. The host pool uses the
+existing HiCache sizing and eviction policies. Staging allocations are separate
+from the host pool; their size depends on the page geometry. Pageable copies
+can synchronize the submitting thread, so timing results from pinned-memory
+HiCache do not describe this mode.

+"""Bounded staging for pageable MLA page-first-direct host transfers.
+
+Write-back packs on the GPU; read-back gathers pageable rows on the CPU.
+Both preserve [page, layer, token, byte] layout and never dereference or
+register host memory from a GPU kernel.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+def transfer_pageable_dsv4_tokens(
+    host, device_buffers, host_indices, device_indices, *, layer=None
+):
+    """Copy partial V4 rows through bounded, ordinary tensor copies.
+
+    ``layer=None`` backs up all layers; an integer restores that layer. Only
+    device tensors participate in GPU indexing. Blocking copies fence the CPU
+    gather/scatter, including when host registration is unavailable.
+    """
+    page_size, value_bytes, scale_bytes = 64, 576, 8
+    page_bytes = 37440
+    if host.device.type != "cpu" or host.shape[-1] != page_bytes:
+        raise ValueError("partial pageable transfers require the DSV4 V4 row layout")
+    if host_indices.numel() != device_indices.numel():
+        raise ValueError("partial pageable transfer index size mismatch")
+    host_rows = host.view(host.shape[0], host.shape[1], page_bytes)
+    hi = host_indices.to(device="cpu", dtype=torch.long)
+    device_cpu = device_indices.to(device="cpu", dtype=torch.long)
+    if hi.numel() and (int(hi.min()) < 0 or int(hi.max()) >= host.shape[0] * page_size):
+        raise ValueError("partial pageable host index out of bounds")
+    layers = range(len(device_buffers)) if layer is None else (layer,)
+    for l in layers:
+        buf = device_buffers[l]
+        if not buf.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError(
+                "partial pageable transfers require contiguous device rows"
+            )
+        dev = buf.view(torch.uint8).view(-1, page_bytes)
+        if device_cpu.numel() and (
+            int(device_cpu.min()) < 0
+            or int(device_cpu.max()) >= dev.shape[0] * page_size
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("partial pageable device index out of bounds")
+        di = device_cpu.to(device=buf.device)
+        # At most 1024 * 576 bytes of payload per layer/component per copy.
+        for begin in range(0, hi.numel(), 1024):
+            h = hi[begin : begin + 1024]
+            d = di[begin : begin + 1024]
+            for base, width in (
+                (0, value_bytes),
+                (page_size * value_bytes, scale_bytes),
+            ):
+                columns = torch.arange(width, device="cpu")
+                hc = base + (h % page_size)[:, None] * width + columns
+                dc = base + (d % page_size)[:, None] * width + columns.to(buf.device)
+                hr, dr = (h // page_size)[:, None], (d // page_size)[:, None]
+                if layer is None:
+                    host_rows[hr, l, hc] = dev[dr, dc].to("cpu", non_blocking=False)
+                else:
+                    dev[dr, dc] = host_rows[hr, l, hc].to(
+                        buf.device, non_blocking=False
+                    )
+        di.record_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(buf.device))

+
+@triton.jit
+def _pack_pages(
+    ptrs,
+    indices,
+    packed,
+    PAGE: tl.constexpr,
+    ROW: tl.constexpr,
+    LAYERS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    page = tl.program_id(0)
+    layer = tl.program_id(1)
+    x = tl.program_id(2) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = x < PAGE * ROW
+    token = tl.load(indices + page * PAGE + x // ROW, mask, other=0)
+    src = tl.load(ptrs + layer).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8))
+    data = tl.load(src + token.to(tl.int64) * ROW + x % ROW, mask, other=0)
+    offset = ((page.to(tl.int64) * LAYERS + layer) * PAGE * ROW) + x
+    tl.store(packed + offset, data, mask)

+def contiguous_page_runs(pages):
+    """Yield source offsets and destination spans without sorting page order."""
+    begin = 0
+    for end in range(1, len(pages) + 1):
+        if end == len(pages) or pages[end] != pages[end - 1] + 1:
+            yield begin, end, pages[begin]
+            begin = end

+class StagedDirectBackup:
+    def __init__(self, host, page_size, device, max_bytes=64 * 1024 * 1024):
+        assert host.device.type == "cpu" and host.is_contiguous()
+        self.page_size = page_size
+        self.layers = host.shape[1]
+        self.row_bytes = host[0, 0, 0].numel() * host.element_size()
+        self.page_bytes = self.layers * page_size * self.row_bytes
+        self.capacity = max(1, min(64, max_bytes // self.page_bytes))
+        self.host = host.view(torch.uint8).view(host.shape[0], self.page_bytes)
+        self.packed = torch.empty(
+            (self.capacity, self.page_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+        )
+
+    def backup(self, ptrs, host_indices, device_indices):
+        # Host allocation supplies complete aligned pages. Check before issuing
+        # any copy, so malformed destinations cannot overwrite adjacent pages.
+        if host_indices.device.type != "cpu":
+            raise ValueError("staged direct backup requires CPU host indices")
+        n = host_indices.numel()
+        if n != device_indices.numel() or n % self.page_size:
+            raise ValueError("staged direct backup requires complete matching pages")
+        if not n:
+            return
+        rows = host_indices.reshape(-1, self.page_size)
+        starts = rows[:, 0]
+        expected = starts[:, None] + torch.arange(self.page_size)
+        if (
+            not torch.equal(rows, expected)
+            or bool((starts % self.page_size).any())
+            or int(starts.min()) < 0
+            or int(starts.max()) // self.page_size >= self.host.shape[0]
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("invalid staged direct destination pages")
+        pages = (starts // self.page_size).tolist()
+        if len(set(pages)) != len(pages):
+            raise ValueError("duplicate staged direct destination pages")
+        indices = device_indices.to(self.packed.device).contiguous()
+        for begin in range(0, len(pages), self.capacity):
+            chunk = pages[begin : begin + self.capacity]
+            _pack_pages[
+                (
+                    len(chunk),
+                    self.layers,
+                    triton.cdiv(self.page_size * self.row_bytes, 1024),
+                )
+            ](
+                ptrs,
+                indices[begin * self.page_size :],
+                self.packed,
+                self.page_size,
+                self.row_bytes,
+                self.layers,
+                1024,
+            )
+            for lo, hi, dst in contiguous_page_runs(chunk):
+                self.host[dst : dst + hi - lo].copy_(
+                    self.packed[lo:hi], non_blocking=True
+                )
+        # The caller owns a single D2H stream and fences pool reuse. Track the
+        # temporary indices on that stream; packed storage persists with pool.
+        indices.record_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(self.packed.device))
+
+
+class StagedDirectLoad:
+    """Gather pageable host rows, then upload and scatter one layer at a time.
+
+    All GPU accesses target device allocations. The blocking H2D copy is
+    intentional: the CPU staging buffer must be reusable on the next layer,
+    including on systems where host memory cannot be pinned or registered.
+    The caller serializes calls on its load stream, including packed drafts.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, host, page_size, device, max_bytes=64 * 1024 * 1024):
+        if host.device.type != "cpu" or not host.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError("staged direct load requires a contiguous CPU pool")
+        self.page_size = page_size
+        self.row_bytes = host[0, 0].numel() * host.element_size() // page_size
+        self.host = host.view(torch.uint8).reshape(
+            host.shape[0], host.shape[1], page_size * self.row_bytes
+        )
+        self.capacity = max(1, max_bytes // (page_size * self.row_bytes))
+        self.device = device
+        self.cpu = self.gpu = None
+
+    def load(self, dst, host_indices, device_indices, layer):
+        n = host_indices.numel()
+        if host_indices.device.type != "cpu":
+            raise ValueError("staged direct load requires CPU host indices")
+        if n != device_indices.numel() or n % self.page_size:
+            raise ValueError("staged direct load requires complete matching pages")
+        if not n:
+            return
+        rows = host_indices.reshape(-1, self.page_size)
+        starts = rows[:, 0]
+        if not torch.equal(
+            rows, starts[:, None] + torch.arange(self.page_size, device="cpu")
+        ) or bool((starts % self.page_size).any()):
+            raise ValueError("invalid staged direct source pages")
+        pages = (starts // self.page_size).long()
+        capacity = min(pages.numel(), self.capacity)
+        if self.cpu is None or self.cpu.shape[0] < capacity:
+            self.cpu = torch.empty(
+                (capacity, self.page_size * self.row_bytes),
+                dtype=torch.uint8,
+                device="cpu",
+                pin_memory=False,
+            )
+            self.gpu = torch.empty_like(self.cpu, device=self.device)
+        indices = device_indices.to(self.device, dtype=torch.long)
+        dst_bytes = dst.view(torch.uint8).view(-1, self.row_bytes)
+        for begin in range(0, pages.numel(), capacity):
+            count = min(capacity, pages.numel() - begin)
+            cpu = self.cpu[:count]
+            gpu = self.gpu[:count]
+            torch.index_select(
+                self.host[:, layer], 0, pages[begin : begin + count], out=cpu
+            )
+            gpu.copy_(cpu, non_blocking=False)
+            offset = begin * self.page_size
+            dst_bytes.index_copy_(
+                0,
+                indices[offset : offset + count * self.page_size],
+                gpu.view(-1, self.row_bytes),
+            )
+        indices.record_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(self.device))

+
+Use an idle HiCache server with cache reports, an 8192-token device KV pool,
+and a host/device ratio of 4. The reference endpoint uses the same model and
+launch configuration without HiCache. Needle prompts follow the Qwen model

+

+

+    session = requests.Session()
+    records = []
+    cases = []
+

+        args.output.write_text(
+            json.dumps(
+                {"passed": passed, "cases": cases, "responses": records}, indent=2
+            )
+        )
+
+    def generate(endpoint, text, max_tokens=64):
+        response = session.post(
+            endpoint + "/generate",
+            json={
+                "text": text,
+                "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": max_tokens},
+            },
+            timeout=600,
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        data = response.json()
+        records.append({"endpoint": endpoint, "response": data})
+        save()
+        return data
+
+    filler = "Archive note: the weather was mild and no unusual event was reported.\n"
+    repeats = args.prompt_tokens // len(tokenizer.encode(filler))
+    for case, depth in enumerate((0.1, 0.5, 0.9)):
+        for endpoint in (args.url, args.reference_url):
+            session.post(endpoint + "/flush_cache", timeout=180).raise_for_status()
+        before = int(repeats * depth)
+        code = str(739391 + case)
+        document = (
+            filler * before
+            + f"IMPORTANT RECORD: The access code is {code}.\n"
+            + filler * (repeats - before)
+        )
+        prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+            [
+                {
+                    "role": "user",
+                    "content": "One of these records contains an access code.\n"
+                    + document
+                    + "\nWhat is the access code? Reply with the digits only.",
+                }
+            ],
+            tokenize=False,
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            enable_thinking=False,
+        )

+                args.url,
+                f"Filler {case}-{i}. "
+                + (f"Unique filler {case}-{i} about an unrelated subject. " * 300),
+                8,
+            )
+        reloaded = generate(args.url, prompt)
+        resident = generate(args.reference_url, prompt)
+        host_hits = (reloaded["meta_info"].get("cached_tokens_details") or {}).get(
+            "host", 0
+        )

+                "depth": depth,
+                "expected": code,
+                "host_tokens": host_hits,

+            }

+        for response in (resident, reloaded):

+            )
